summary: Reproduced the eager OLMo-2 QK norm bypass and changed the non-capture branch to use normal RMSNorm dispatch. On the assigned MI350X this selected the real AITER kernel, matched independent FP64 references across relevant layouts and dtypes, and replayed correctly from a real ROCm graph.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: eager branch bypassed module dispatch and called forward_native; capture branch already dispatched.
Passing-after regression for eager dispatch and capture-only alternate-stream behavior.
Real forward_aiter RMSNorm on MI350X versus an independent FP64 reference for BF16/FP16/FP32 and contiguous/QKV-split layouts.

tests.command: SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-29840765b7c7/venv/bin/python < branch and ROCm graph harness
tests.what_was_measured: Eager public dispatch, graph-capture branch, replay without Python re-entry, and replay numerical equivalence.
Focused two-norm microbenchmark only: AITER versus decomposed native at 1, 128, and 16384 tokens; not full-model timing.

gpu_execution_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X; real AITER RMSNorm shared objects loaded from /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-29840765b7c7/cache/aiter; ROCm graph capture/replay and numerical harness logs retained.
remaining_limitations: No OLMo-2 weights: full-model serving, semantic accuracy, and end-to-end prefill/decode timing were unavailable.
No NVIDIA H200 was assigned; upstream H200 measurements were not reproduced.
The unrelated CUDA FA3 illegal-address failure was kept out of scope.
No SGLang/FlyDSL native source changed and repository-environment.json supplied no native rebuild target.
